subsystems.name: Brain preservation
subsystems.role: stabilise the brain's structure so it can be scanned without decay.

subsystems.name: Nanoscale imaging
subsystems.role: capture every neuron, synapse and process at nanometre resolution.

subsystems.name: Connectome reconstruction
subsystems.role: turn raw images into a complete wiring diagram of the brain.

subsystems.name: Neural simulation
subsystems.role: run a computational model of the brain's neurons and synapses.

subsystems.name: Sensory and motor interface
subsystems.role: connect the simulated mind to a virtual or robotic body.

subsystems.name: Data storage and compute
subsystems.role: store and process the enormous datasets and real-time simulation.

buildSteps.title: Preserve a brain
buildSteps.detail: After death, or from a living donor under extreme ethical constraints, perfuse the brain with chemical fixatives or cryoprotectants to lock proteins and membranes in place.

buildSteps.title: Slice and image
buildSteps.detail: Cut the brain into nanometre-thin sections and image each one with electron microscopy, capturing every neuron, axon and synapse.

buildSteps.title: Reconstruct the connectome
buildSteps.detail: Use machine-learning algorithms to trace neurons and synapses across the images, then manually proofread to correct errors.

buildSteps.title: Infer functional parameters
buildSteps.detail: From synapse size, type and location, estimate connection strengths, neuron types and other properties needed for a realistic model.

buildSteps.title: Build a computational model
buildSteps.detail: Create a software replica of every neuron and synapse, with equations that approximate their electrical and chemical behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Simulate and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Run the model on a supercomputer, compare its activity patterns to recorded brain activity from the original, and adjust until it matches.

buildSteps.title: Interface and embody
buildSteps.detail: Give the simulation sensory input and a way to act, so it can interact with a virtual world or a robotic body.

buildSteps.title: Validate identity
buildSteps.detail: Test for memory, personality and continuity of self; this remains philosophically unresolved and may never be fully provable.

prerequisites.tech: Synaptic-resolution connectomics of a human brain
prerequisites.why: current methods are destructive and too slow; mapping a whole human brain at this detail is far beyond present capability.
simulating about 86 billion neurons with trillions of synapses in real time would need vastly more compute than today's fastest machines.
we do not yet know how patterns of neural activity produce thoughts, memories or consciousness.
cryopreservation damages tissue; chemical fixation preserves structure but kills the brain.
needed to connect a simulated mind to sensors and actuators, but current bandwidth is very limited.

pathway.milestone: complete connectomes of small organisms such as the nematode C. elegans and larval fruit fly, plus macro-scale human maps
pathway.unlocks: methods for tracing neural wiring and handling large datasets.

pathway.milestone: synaptic-resolution map of a mouse brain and simulation of simple circuits, tested against real neural activity
pathway.unlocks: evidence that structure can predict function at small scale.

pathway.milestone: partial human brain emulation, such as a cortical column, with some functional validation
pathway.unlocks: proof that human tissue can be modelled and simulated meaningfully.

pathway.milestone: whole human brain emulation at real-time speed, if computing and neuroscience advance enough
pathway.unlocks: a digital replica that could, in theory, support a mind.

pathway.milestone: transfer of a person's consciousness to a digital substrate
pathway.unlocks: nothing guaranteed; it remains unproven and may be impossible.
